The bottom club would be relegated to the [[Thailand Division 1 League]]. The club that came 11th would play in a relegation / promotion match against the club that came second in the [[Thailand Division 1 League]] Defending Champions [[Royal Thai Air Force FC|Royal Thai Air Force]] should have entered the next edition of the [[Asian Club Championship]], but refused due to lack of funding. [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] took their place. 2nd head-to-head; 3rd goal difference; 4th goals scored }} == Promotion and relegation Playoff == The club that came 11th would play in a relegation / promotion match against the runner-up in the [[Thailand Division 1 League]]. January 24 and January 31, 1998 {| border="1" cellpadding="4" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:center; border-collapse:collapse;" |- style="background:#efefef;" ! Team 1 ! Result ! Team 2 |- style="" | † [[Rattana Bundit FC|Bangkok Metropolitan Administration]] | 3-1 | [[Sriracha FC|Assumption Sriracha]] |} † [[Rattana Bundit FC|Bangkok Metropolitan Administration]] remain at the [[Thai Premier League]]. == Season notes == * The bottom club would be relegated, with the team coming 11th, to play in a relegation / promotion matchup against the 2nd placed team in [[Thailand Division 1 League]]. * [[Raj Pracha FC|UCOM Raj Pracha]] were relegated and replaced by 2nd level winners Bangkok Bank of Commerce. * [[Rattana Bundit FC|Bangkok Metropolitan Administration]] overcame [[Sriracha FC|Assumption Sriracha]] in the playoff match. * [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|Tero Sasana]] changed the club's name again to [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] with the main sponsor, Thailand’s Entertainment giant "'''BEC Tero Entertainment'''." ==Queens Cup== The Singha sponsored [[Queen's Cup (football)|Queen's Cup]] was postponed because of lack of sponsorship, will be held next year but with reduced prize money. ==Thailand FA Cup== [[Bangkok Bank FC|Bangkok Bank]] won the 1998 [[Thailand FA Cup]], and their 3rd victory in this competition. It is unclear whom they beat in the final ==Yamaha Thailand Cup== '''1998''' saw the 14th edition of the '''Yamaha Thailand Cup'''. It was Thailand's main inter-provincial competition, played between qualifiers from various regions. The first round saw four groups of four teams, of which the top two sides qualified for the Quarter-Final knockout stage. [[Rattana Bundit FC|Bangkok Metropolitan Administration]] beat [[Nakhon Si Thammarat]] in the final. ==Asian Representation== * [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] represented Thailand in the [[1998–99 Asian Club Championship]], where they would reach the second round, beaten by Chinese opposition in [[Dalian Wanda]], the same club who ended [[Bangkok Bank FC|Bangkok Bank]]'s adventure the previous year. * [[Sinthana FC|Sinthana]] made the second round of the [[1998–99 Asian Cup Winners Cup]], where they were out classed by Japanese opposition in [[Kashima Antlers]]. == Annual awards == === Coach of the Year === *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Karoon Narksawat]] - [[Sinthana FC|Sinthana]] === Player of the Year === *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Niweat Siriwong]] - [[Sinthana FC|Sinthana]] === Top scorer === *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Ronnachai Sayomchai]] - 23 Goals[[Football records in Thailand]] [[Port Authority of Thailand FC|Port Authority of Thailand]] ==Champions== The champion for the 1998 season was [[BBCU F.C.|Sinthana]].
